Track Bulletins 
UP Trains between Polo and Airline Jct. 
Southward UP trains must obtain TGBO at Des 
Moines.  Northward trains must obtain TGBO at the 
originating terminal, unless otherwise instructed. 
 
TrAM Area 
The Kansas City Sub is: 
TrAM Area 1 between MP 302.8 and MP 405.1. 
TrAM Area 2 between MP 405.1 and MP 498.8. 
 
Block System 
Centralized Traffic Control is in use between Laredo 
and Airline Jct. 
 
Movement Authority 
Track Warrant Control is in use between Ottumwa and 
to Laredo North. 
 
Main Track Designation 
Two main tracks are in use between Polo and Airline 
Jct, except over Drawbridge.  Beginning at the west, 
the main tracks are numbered 1 and 2. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Interlocking 
Automatic Interlocking - APNC JCT . To enter CP 
main track within automatic interlocking limits, 
employees must not open the case door or unlock  
electrically locked switch without Track Warrant 
authority from CP Operations Supervisor. 
Employees must not operate Maintenance of Way Lock 
Box without permission from CP Operations 
Supervisor. 
 
Birmingham - Manual interlocking under the control of 
the NS KN Tower control operator. 
 
Drawbridge - Manual interlocking at MP 497.0 under 
the control of the CP Operation Supervisor. 
 
Equipment Restrictions 
Kansas City Terminal: Close clearance in East Yard 
(EYD) track 100 (short 1) – south side only, track 101 
(1 track) – north and south side and track 102 (2 
track) – north side only, will not clear man on side of 
equipment.  
 
Switch Information 
Liberty - The inside switch at the South end of the 
Center siding must be lined and locked for movement 
onto the NO 2 Main Track. The inside switch at the 
North end of the Center siding must be lined and locked 
for movement onto the NO 1 Main Track. 
 
The following main track switches may be left lined 
and locked in either position: 
  
Ottumwa - North switch at Quincy Street

General Information 
Ottumwa - BNSF crews using CP track must monitor 
the CP road channel 044-044. 
 
Laredo - Elevator track numbers 1, 2 and MFA track 
only are in service.  No loaded cars may be placed on 
No. 2 Track.   Due to close clearance crews must not 
ride sides of cars between 1 and 2 tracks when cars 
are located on those tracks. 
  
Laredo - When using the inside crossover switch for 
track protection while working on the Stub track at 
Laredo, you must contact the Dispatcher and inform 
them that you will be lining the switch for protection 
account of the switch, when thrown reverse, will give a 
track occupancy indication on the Dispatchers 
computer. Once the switch is no longer needed for 
protection, it must be lined back for the stub track to 
yard track movement. 
 
Lucerne - Premium Standard Farms (PSF) is 
designated a REMOTE-CONTROL ZONE (RCZ). 
CP crews must contact PSF on radio channel AAR 
044-044 for permission to enter the RCZ. When work 
is completed and are clear of the RCZ, they will notify 
PSF.  
  
If unable to contact PSF by radio, notify the Operations 
Supervisor and request Customer Service contact 
PSF. 
 
Joint Agency Yard - Joint Agency limits include all 
tracks other than CP Main Track. Employees are 
required to have a current copy of the Greater Kansas 
City Operating Instructions and KCS Timetable and 
Special Instructions.

General Information 
CLARK  
WWD Trains holding main track at Clark to meet EWD 
trains must stop east of posted point East of MP 351.5 
until EWD train clear of main track. 
 
ROCK CREEK JCT  
Trains exceeding 3,700 feet do not foul crossing at 
Independence Ave. MP 480.95 until instructed by KCT,  
Traffic Control Operator Kansas City to proceed to 
Rock Creek Jct. 
 
KANSAS CITY  
While operating on trackage of foreign lines in the 
Kansas City area, all employees will be governed by 
the current edition of the Greater Kansas City Area 
Operating Rules and Special Instructions. 
 
OZARK VALLEY RAILROAD  
MP 326.1 - All movement governed by GCOR Rule 
6.28.  
 
The Ozark Valley Railroad begins operations at MP 0.0 
to MP 24.8 (end of track) on the former Mexico 
Industrial Lead (Fulton Branch).  
 
INSTRUCTIONS FOR CROSSING NS RR AT 
MEXICO, MO, TO ENTER OZARK VALLEY RR  
Contact NS Dispatcher on radio channel 031 -031 and 
tone 355, to receive permission to crossover. 
 
BROKEN RAIL DETECTION (BRD)  
Broken Rail Detection (BRD) limits are in effect on the 
main track between MP 480.9 and MP 327.4.  
 
Begin BRD and End BRD signs will be posted at the 
outer limits of BRD Territory.  
 
Limits monitored by BRD have indicators that display  
aspects for the condition of the track. 
 
BRD INDICATORS  
Aspect  Indication  
Flashing Green  No defects.  
Flashing Red  Expect next indicator to be red.  
Red or Dark  Proceed at restricted speed until the 
leading wheels pass the next BRD 
indicator and report to the train 
dispatcher. 
 
While moving within BRD territory, trains must comply 
with the indication of the BRD indicator.

General Information 
Trains Departing Kansas City  
CPKC southward trains will contact the yardmaster for 
permission to depart. Once permission from 
yardmaster is granted, train will then contact CPKC 
dispatcher for permission to enter CPKC dispatched 
Main Track at KCS JCT. Once permission is received 
from CPKC dispatcher, the train is to contact KCT East 
dispatcher and report the following: Train ID; 
Locomotive number; total number of cars; tonnage; 
footage (including locomotives); from location (e.g., 
902) and to location (e.g., CPKC Main Track).  
 
Trains Departing Kansas City Off the K CT Main 
Track  
CPKC southward trains departing off the KCT Main 
Track (aka bridge 19 meets) after reporting to KCT that 
crew is on train. Crew will contact CPKC dispatcher for 
permission to enter CPKC Main Track at KCS Jct. If 
unable to contact either CPKC or KCT dispatcher call 
CPKC Yardmaster and report situation.  
 
Trains Arriving Kansas City  
Before passing signal at North Blue Valley NWD  
movements must comply with the following.  
• Trains must report locomotive/train ID and total  
cars in train to CPKC yardmaster and receive  
instructions.  
• The crew must contact KCT East dispatcher to enter  
KCT track. The crew will inform the KCT East  
dispatcher of the following: Train ID; Locomotive  
number; total number of cars (loads, empties)  
tonnage; footage (including locomotives); from  
location (e.g., Blue Valley) and to location (e.g.  
Knoche, BNSF Murray yard, etc.)  
 
All trains and locomotives entering Kansas City yard  
limits must operate on radio channel 064-064. Prior to  
entering Kansas City yard limits, you must contact the  
yardmaster for instructions and to ascertain route is 
clear. Do not foul the west end of any track at East 
Kansas City yard until receiving permission from the 
yardmaster.  
 
Industrial lead must have a minimum of two cars 
coupled together south of Front Street when leaving 
equipment unattended.   
 
US Southern Region Timetable  
PITTSBURG SUBDIVISION  25  July 1, 2024 
 
 
Close Clearances not otherwise specified in the 
timetable are designated by Close Clearance Signs, 
crews are to use caution when handling equipment at 
any location where close clearances may exist.   
 
CPKC crews operating on Kansas City Terminal 
trackage will use KCT Channel 060-060.  
 
While operating on trackage of foreign lines in the 
Kansas City area, all employees will be governed by 
the current edition of the Greater Kansas City 
Operating Rules and Special Instructions.  
 
When operating solid over -the-road trains from the 
CPKC to BNSF, the following will govern:  
• When a train is routed via the Kansas City Terminal  
Railway, notify the Kansas City Tower of the arriving  
and departure time at KCS junction.  
• Notify the Kansas City Tower when arriving Airline  
Junction to obtain a route and clearance to the  
BNSF.  
• Notify the Kansas City Tower when arriving on the  
KCT Bluff Track, and again when departing the KCT  
Bluff Track.  
• When arriving Harlem Street or Ustic Tower, call the  
Kansas City Tower to request transportation from the  
BNSF yard and advise the delivery time.  
• Any delay in excess of fifteen minutes en route to the  
BNSF must be reported at once to the Kansas City  
Yardmaster. If delay continues, a status report must  
be made every fifteen minutes to permit supervisors  
to handle.  
 
Maintenance of Way employees desiring to perform 
track work on the main track between MP 5.0 and MP 
6.3 must obtain permission from the KCT Operator.  
 
Kansas City Terminal  
Close clearance in East Yard (EYD) track 100 (short 1) 
– south side only, track 101 (1 track) – north and south 
side and track 102 (2 track) – north side only, will not 
clear man on side of equipment.  
 
The group of tracks 4 through 20 within Knoche Yard is 
designated as bowl tracks, tracks 4 through 20 must be 
secured with three hand brakes on each track. Crews 
must leave behind the three cars with hand brakes 
unless otherwise directed by the Knoche Yardmaster.  
 
Industrial lead switch must be left lined for 903 when 
not in use. West end of the service track must be lined 
for 902 when not in use.  
 
Road crews departing the service track will operate on  
radio channel 064 -064 within the Kansas City yard 
limits (Knoche Yard) until train is released and 
departing yard limits.  
 
Crews delivering trains to foreign line carriers will use 
radio channel 064 -064 to contact the yardmaster to 
arrange transportation.  
 
Bulk commodity trains do not use the crossover 901 to 
the north Main Track at Kansas Avenue.  
 
Unit oil trains are restricted to Tracks 901, 902 and 903.  
 
 
 
 
 
Remote Operations:  
The Kansas City Joint Agency Yard has been 
established as a Remote-Control Operating Area.  
 
A Remote-Control Zone is established in the Kansas 
City Joint Agency Yard on the work lead between the 
East G.I. Track switch extending Eastward to the 
Eastbound clearance point of the track 125 switch.   
This zone shall be identified as RCZ 1.   
 
A Remote-Control Zone is established in the Kansas 
City Joint Agency Yard on the work lead between the 
Eastbound clearance point of the track 125 -switch 
extending Eastward to the clearance point of the Zero 
Track switch. This zone shall be identified as RCZ 2.   
 
A Remote-Control Zone is established in the Kansas 
City Joint Agency Yard on Zero Track between the 
work lead/ west crossover switch extending Eastward 
to the clearance point of the Tail Track switch. This 
zone shall be identified as RCZ 3. 
 
Drexel  
When possible, southward trains stop at least 720 feet 
north of Pine Street, MP 53.0, when leaving train 
unattended, waiting for signal indication or waiting to 
meet opposing train.  
 
Amsterdam  
A dual control derail is installed at the clearance point 
of the North leg of the Wye. This derail operates in  
conjunction with the dual controlled switch at 
Amsterdam Wye. When operating the Amsterdam Wye 
dual control switch by hand, it is also necessary to 
operate the derail by hand.  
 
IFG  
Permission must be granted by CPKC Console 1 
Dispatcher prior to occupying Business Track (602) at 
IFG. CPKC Console 1 Dispatcher must be informed 
once movement is clear of Business Track (602) at 
IFG.  
 
A dual-control derail is installed at the south end of IFG. 
This derail operates in conjunction with the dual -
controlled main line switch. When operating the South 
IFG dual-controlled switch by hand, it is also necessary 
to operate the derail by hand.  
 
The practice of mounting and dismounting moving 
equipment on Track 201 within the International Freight 
Gateway ("IFG") facility is prohibited. 
 
---END---

Heavener  
A dual control derail on the south lead at Heavener yard 
is located 345 feet north of the No. 1 (East) main switch 
and operates in conjunction with the No. 1 (East) main 
track. When operating the No. 1 (East) main switch by 
hand, it will also be necessary to operate the derail by 
hand.  
 
Empire  
An interlocked dual-controlled derail is installed at the 
clearance point of Empire. This derail operates in 
conjunction with the dual-controlled switch operated by 
the train dispatcher. When operating the Empire dual -
controlled switch by hand, it is also necessary to 
operate the derail by hand.

Train crews operating empty coal trains will perform a 
Class IA air brake test prior to departure.  
 
Joplin  
Northward trains encountering a STOP indication at the 
MNA automatic interlocking, MP 154.8 will also receive 
a dark signal at the south siding switch at Joplin until 
the engine occupies the MNA interlocking limits.  
 
Simmons Industry  
A) Cars must not be left between the main track switch 
and the switch point derail, which is located 554 feet 
from the main track switch.  
B) Crew members are prohibited from riding  
equipment within the dumper room.  
 
Flint Creek  
A power operated switch point derail is installed at the 
clearance point of the Flint Creek Spur. This derail 
operates in conjunction with the dual -controlled Flint 
Creek Spur switch operated by the train dispatcher. 
When operating the Flint Creek dual -controlled switch 
by hand, it is also necessary to operate the derail by 
hand.  
 
Train crews operating empty coal trains will perform a 
Class IA air brake test prior to departure.  
 
Footing At 253.2 and 263.6  
Train crews are prohibited from walking on the right of 
way at the following locations:  
• MP 253.2 - East side of main track  
• MP 263.6 - East side of main track  
 
Sallisaw  
The interlocking signals at the UP crossing are also  
designated as a control point. When a crew encounters 
a STOP signal at this location and fails to receive  a 
proceed indication after following instructions in the 
release box, authority must be received from the train 
dispatcher before proceeding except when operating 
within the limits of track and time.  
 
Waldron Industrial Spur (MP 0.0 To MP 4.0)  
All movements must be made per Rule 6.28 not to  
exceed 10 MPH on all tracks. MP 4.0 begins Arkansas 
Southern Railroad.  
 
OK Feed  
1. Riding on the sides of engines or cars while entering 
or moving through the dumper facility is prohibited. 
Train crews must remain inside the locomotive cab.  
2. Speed through the dumper room and over the  
scales is restricted to 5 MPH.

General Information 
 
Page - Mena  
The sighting of fire between Page and Mena must be  
reported immediately to the train dispatcher.  
 
Hatfield  
Between North and South Switches Pass Track, a 
switch point derail has been installed 341 feet north of 
the south switch.  
 
Hatton  
Train crews must have the automatic brakes cut in and  
operative on all cars when switching the rock plants at  
Hatton. Cars stored or spotted for loading must be left  
with the air brakes applied, wheels chocked, and  
sufficient hand brakes applied to prevent movement.  
 
 
 
 
A dual control switch has been installed on the main 
track MP 405 for entrance to south leg of the wye. A 
power switch point derail has been installed 
approximately 300 ft. from the dual control switch on 
the south leg of the wye and operates in conjunctio n 
with the dual control main track switch. When 
permission is received to operate the dual control 
switch by hand, it will also be necessary to operate the 
switch point derail by hand.  
 
When picking up cars, hand brakes will not be released  
until after Air Brake Test is completed.  
 
Before departing Hatton Rock plant:  
• If train contains less than 50% MWAX type 
equipment make a minimum automatic brake 
reduction, release hand brakes, and move 
train WITHOUT releasing minimum set.  
• If train contains at least 50% MWAX type 
equipment, move train with automatic brake 
released. Use dynamic or automatic brake 
applications as necessary to control train.  
 
When taking a Distributed Power train into the plant, 
crews must end distributed power on both ends before 
leaving the train at Hatton.

798-2871 from 06:00 to 18:00 or the Longview

However, the crossover at North Shreveport must not 
be used in hand throw position without authority on the 
East Main. Trains and switch jobs have permission to 
change directions within the limits of the control point 
at North Shreveport between the switching signals if 
the crossover is not used. If the switching signal is 
displaying a STOP indication, ensure the switch from 
the run around is lined for your desired move, and if 
signal still displays a STOP indication, trains and switch 
crews must contact the Shreveport Terminal 
Yardmaster for instructions. However, if the control 
point is occupied by its own standing train or  cut of 
cars, the train or switch job may, after stopping, pass  
the switching signal displaying STOP indication without  
contacting the Shreveport Terminal Yardmaster.  
 
North Lead 29 Switch is close clearance on the west 
side of the North 30 Lead.   
 
The North switching lead between CP 550 (MP 550.2) 
and MP 551.9 is 20 MPH.  
 
A Switch Point Indicator has been installed at the  
Shreveport Industrial Switch, MP 551.1 on the Tail 
Track. The switch point indicator as defined by GCOR 
Rule 8.10 will indicate the switch positions as follows:  
 
GREEN light will indicate switch points fit properly in 
normal position.  
YELLOW light will indicate switch points fit properly in 
reverse position.  
RED or DARK  light will indicate stop and inspect 
switch.  
 
South Shreveport Yard  
The signals at the South end of Shreveport yard that 
govern movement northward from Hollywood 1 and 
southward from zero track, with the exception of the 
signal governing movement through the crossover 
from zero track at South Shreveport, will be referred to 
as ‘switching signals. If the switching signal is 
displaying a restricting indication, the train or switch job 
has permission to use the signals for movement in the 
control point. However, the dual control switch at the 
crossover must not be used in hand throw position 
without authority on Hollywood 2. Tra ins and switch 
jobs have permission to change directions within the 
limits of the control point at South Shreveport between 
the switching signals if  the crossover switch is not 
used. If the switching signal is displaying a STOP 
indication, trains and switch crews must contact the 
Shreveport Terminal Yardmaster for instructions. 
However, if the control point is occupied by its own 
standing train or cut of cars, the train or switch job may, 
after stopping, pass the switching signal displaying 
STOP indication without contacting the Shreveport 
Terminal Yardmaster.  
 
CP 556 (Hollywood 1)  
A dual control derail is installed on the north industry 
track. This derail operates in conjunction with the 
main line switch. When operating the dual control 
switch by hand, it is also necessary to operate the 
split point derail by hand.  
 
 
 
 
Harriet Street Yard  
DTMF Yard Switches are installed on both ends of 
Harriet Street Yard. When entering the North or South 
End of Harriet Street yard, it will be necessary to 
operate the DTMF yard switches.   
North Lead Track switch code: normal switch DTMF  
#556311 – reverse DTMF # 556322.   
South Lead Track switch code: normal switch DTMF  
#557211 – reverse DTMF #557222.  
 
The switch point indicator will indicate the following:  
Green - normal position (Lead to Lead)  
Yellow - reverse position (Lead to L 1)  
Red - in transition or out of correspondence  
 
NOTE: There is a 50 ft. to 100 ft. circuit at these 
switches that must not be fouled until the switch is lined 
for intended movement. 
 
Tracks 1, 4, 5 and the lead tracks at north and south 
Harriett Street are 15 MPH. 
 
Spring Switches:  
• L&A Junction, MPB-105.1:  
NWD movement leave lined as last used.  
SWD movement should line switch for UP main 
track and trail through.  
• Louisiana Junction, MPL-561.7:  
Leave lined as last used. 
Power Assisted Switches (PAS): 
Alliance Jct. 
Radio Channel 010-010 
Normal DTMF #580411 Reverse DTMF #580422 
 
General Information 
Track Bulletins:  
• Yard trains  – If required, verify Track Bulletins 
with Shreveport Terminal Yardmaster when going 
on duty.  
• Road Trains  - If required, verify Track Bulletins 
with the train dispatcher.  
 
Universal Oil Products MP 544.9  
Train crews working Universal Oil Products (UOP) at 
Brian, LA must wear approved hardhat while working 
inside the UOP facility.  
 
Cedar Grove Yard  
Trains, engines, and all on track equipment must obtain  
permission from the dispatcher to occupy Cedar Grove  
Yard.    
 
Departure Instructions Shreveport Yard  
Trains, engines, and all on track equipment ready to 
depart Shreveport Yard must obtain permission from 
the Shreveport Terminal Yardmaster before departing.  
• If train or part of train received a Class I Air Brake 
Test at Shreveport Yard, crew must ascertain if a 
Roll-By release of air brakes system is required on 
departure.  
 
Permission To Occupy Tracks Shreveport Terminal  
Hollywood 1 553.5 – 554.7 must not be occupied 
without permission from the Shreveport Terminal 
Yardmaster.   
 
 
 
US Southern Region Timetable  
SHREVEPORT TERMINAL  42  July 1, 2024 
 
 
 
Trains, Engines and All on Track Equip ment 
Departing Shreveport Yard To:  
• Alexandria, Beaumont, Hope Industrial Lead or  
Vicksburg Subdivisions or Other Yards and  
Industries: Must obtain verbal permission to 
proceed to CTC from train dispatcher before 
departing Shreveport Yard. Following receipt of 
authority to enter CTC, contact the Shreveport 
Terminal Yardmaster for permission to proceed to 
CTC.  
 
NOTE: Trains, engines, and all on track equipment en 
route to Alexandria Subdivision must not depart Red 
Junction until after they have been issued a Track 
Warrant.  
 
• Shreveport And Greenville Subdivisions: Must  
obtain verbal permission to proceed to CTC at 
North Shreveport (Main Track Specific) from Train 
Dispatcher prior to departing Shreveport Yard. 
Following receipt of authority to enter CTC, 
contact the Shreveport Terminal Yardmaster for 
permission to proceed to CTC.  
 
Trains, Engines And All On -Track Equipment 
Entering Shreveport Yard From:  
• Beaumont Subdivision And Cedar Grove  
Industrial Areas: Must contact Shreveport 
Terminal Yardmaster before departing Texas 
Avenue.  
• Shreveport And Greenville Subdivision: Must  
contact Shreveport Terminal Yardmaster before  
departing Texas Junction. All southbound trains 
must clear CP North Shreveport before changing 
crews unless authorized by the yardmaster or train 
dispatcher.  
• Shreveport Terminal CTC Limits On #1, #2 and 
#3 Main Tracks : Must contact Shreveport 
Terminal yardmaster prior to arriving Texas Ave.  
• Hope Industrial Lead And Alexandria  
Subdivisions: Before departing L&A Junction or 
Curtis, crew member must contact the train 
dispatcher for permission to proceed. If using Red 
Junction, the crew must contact UP Hollywood 
Yardmaster (077 -077) for permission to use UP 
trackage between Red Junction and L&A Junction. 
If delays are encountered notify the train 
dispatcher. 
 
Operation Via Up For Movement Between Red 
Junction And L&A Junction  
CPKC movement using UP tracks between Red 
Junction and L&A Junction are governed by the CPKC 
General Code of Operating Rules and current UP 
Timetable.  
 
Prior to entering UP trackage between Red Junction 
and L&A Junction, crews must:  
1. Secure UP track Warrant for bulletins.  
2. Contact UP Yardmaster (Channel 077 -077, phone 
318-632-6640)  
3. Verify any track bulletin changes that would affect 
the trains movement as outlined in Rule 6.2.  
 
 
 
 
 
Employees who receive a UP track warrant listing track  
bulletins only (or “None” on line 16) must contact the 
UP-Train Dispatcher (channel 082 -082, press *(star) 
57 to tone train dispatcher, phone 1-800-726-1106) if:  
• Incorrect/incomplete limits are listed on the “From” 
or  
“To” locations of the address  
or  
• The “OK” time is more than 4 hours old. (More than 
4 hours before the time the track warrant was 
received)  
 
Operation Of Foreign Line Trains Over CPKC Main 
Tracks  
All Foreign Line Trains must obtain authority from the 
CPKC train dispatcher before entering the CPKC Main 
Track at Spring Street, CP 558, or Red Junction.  
 
Trains Moving In And Out Of Shreveport Yard  
Between MP 551 and MP 553.7, Loaded Bulk 
Commodity Trains are allowed to only operate over 
East and West MT unless authorized by the Shreveport 
Terminal Superintendent and the Roadmaster. All yard 
tracks will be used for Loaded Bulk Commodity Trains 
only on an exception basis.  
 
Trains operating on the east and west main tracks 
between MP 552.1 and 553.5 should ring engine bell 
continuously. 
 
Shreveport Diesel Shop  
Mechanical Department power operated derails are in  
service on the following tracks north and south of the 
Diesel Shop.  
• On north run -around approximately 1,900 feet 
north of register room.  
• On south run-around at RIP No. 456 switch.  
 
These power operated derails are equipped with blue  
lights. All locomotives and/or train movements will not 
pass the above derail locations unless permission has 
been received from the diesel shop foreman to move 
beyond the derail.  
 
Outbound locomotives from the diesel shop cannot be  
moved until permission has been received from the 
diesel shop foreman.  
 
Inbound locomotives for the diesel shop must call for  
permission from the diesel shop foreman.  
 
Switch 475 at MP 552.4 is Out of Service.  
 
Crew members will place locomotive consist on track  
designated by the diesel shop foreman.  
 
Run-around track must be left lined for run -around 
when not in use.  
 
Train and Enginemen do not get on or off moving  
equipment while inside the north and south derail.  
 
Car Shop  
Close clearance east side of Track 147.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
US Southern Region Timetable  
SHREVEPORT TERMINAL  43  July 1, 2024 
 
 
 
 
Shreveport Yard Complex Entrances  
Entrance gates are numbered as follows:  
• Gate number 1 is the General Office 
Building/Training Center.  
• Gate number 2 is the Diesel Shop, Annex 
Building, Signal area.  
• Gate number 3 is the Car Shop, Wheel Shop, 
Storeroom, Paint Shop area.  
• Gate number 4 is the Trans-Serve area.  
• Gate number 5 is the Yard Office and 
Transportation area.  
• Gate number 6 is on North Lakeshore.  
• Gate number 7 is the CPKC Transport, 
Maintenance of Way, Signal, and Transportation 
area.  
• Isolation gate is on North Lakeshore Drive 
access to north end of yard.  
 
NOTE: All gates must remain closed when not in use.  
 
Emergency Instructions  
When calling emergency vehicles to the Shreveport 
Yard complex, the following outline should be used to 
help expedite their arrival:  
1. Call 911 immediately and remain calm.  
2. Identify yourself (name) and that you are at CPKC  
(Canadian Pacific Kansas City Railway), Shreveport 
Yard, 4601 Hilry Huckaby III Avenue, Louisiana 
Highway 173, Shreveport, Louisiana.  
3. Give reason for call - Injured person(s); burned, 
heart attack, injury, fire(s) - oil, gas, chemical, etc.,  
explosion(s) - chemical leak(s) - or other.  
4. Give gate number with the most direct access to the  
emergency. If direct access is blocked give next  
easiest access gate number.  
5. Give location of emergency. Example: General 
Office - second floor, or Diesel Shop - south end, or 
near north shanty north end of yard, etc.  
6. Dispatch person(s) to the given gate to direct the  
emergency vehicle to the crisis. If more than one  
response vehicle is expected, dispatched person(s)  
should stay at gate until all emergency vehicles 
arrive. If available, more than one person may be 
needed to perform the task of directing vehicles 
through yard to crisis.  
7. Report incident to all necessary railway supervisors 
and civilian authorities as stated in rule book.  
 
Reporting Delays  
All road and yard crews going on duty in Shreveport  
Terminal (Shreveport Yard, Harriet St., Bossier Yards) 
must report the status of their crew to the Tower no later 
than five (5) minutes after their on -duty time. Yard 
crews must report to the Shreveport Terminal 
Yardmaster through the intercom (talkbacks) or on the 
telephone at ext. 6539. Road crews must report in by 
telephone on ext. 6031 or use ext. 6539 as an 
alternate. Crews should make every attempt to 
immediately secure their train documents at call time.  
Should they not have their required train doc uments 
after being on duty for twenty -five (25) minutes, they 
are again required to report to the tower in the manner 
outlined above.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
In addition, road crews departing the diesel shop 
facilities must notify the Shreveport Terminal 
Yardmaster of any delays encountered commencing 
from call time.  
 
All yard crews (including Bossier local crews) must 
contact the Shreveport Terminal Yardmaster prior to 
tie-up. If any crew is unable to complete their assigned 
work order before the expiration of the hours of service, 
they must  make arrangements with the Shreveport 
Terminal Yardmaster to have work order completed.  
 
Remote Operations  
Shreveport Terminal has been established as a 
Remote-Control Operating Area.  
 
A Remote-Control Zone is established on the north end 
of Shreveport Yard on the north switching lead between 
the one (1) track switch extending northward to the 
clearance point of the run around track. This zone is 
identified as “RCZ 1”.  
 
A Remote-Control Zone is established on the north end 
of Shreveport Yard on the north switching lead between 
the clearance point of the run around track extending 
northward to CP 550. This zone is identified as RCZ 2.  
 
Shreveport Terminal Automated Classification  
Yard  
The group of tracks numbered 1 through 30 within  
Shreveport Yard is designated as bowl tracks. Tracks 
1-12 must be secured with two hand brakes and Tracks 
13-30 must be secured with three hand brakes, 
preferably on the ‘leave behind’ cars.  
 
Crews must ‘leave behind’ the required cars unless  
directed by the Shreveport Terminal Yardmaster. On 
the North switching lead, DO NOT cut off cars in motion 
while in the painted area designated as a “NO Cut 
Zone”. 
 
Milepost Equalization:  
• North Leg Texas Wye (West Main): MP 548.3 on the 
Shreveport Terminal Subdivision and MP Y -548.3 on 
the Shreveport Terminal Subdivision are the same  
location.  
• West Leg Texas Wye:  0.7 on the Greenville 
Subdivision and MP Y -548.7 on the Shreveport 
Terminal Subdivision are the same location.  
• Texas JCT: The southbound signal entering West  
Main off the Greenville Subdivision at MP 0.08 is the  
official Shreveport Terminal – Greenville Subdivision  
boundary.  
Note: Any bulletins requested from the switch point to  
the clearance point within the Texas Jct. turnout in  
Shreveport Terminal must be defined from MP 0.08 to  
MP 0.0 (0.08 is the south bound signal entering West  
Main off the Greenville Subdivision; 0.0 is the switch  
point).  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
US Southern Region Timetable  
SHREVEPORT TERMINAL  44  July 1, 2024 
 
   
 
 
 

US Southern Region Timetable  
SHREVEPORT TERMINAL  45  July 1, 2024 
 
 
 
 
 
 

US Southern Region Timetable  
SHREVEPORT TERMINAL  46  July 1, 2024 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
---END---

Switch Information 
Alliance Junction  
The normal position for the Alliance Jct. Switch is lined 
for the Alliance Subdivision and will display the 
following aspects when moving EWD and WWD:  
 
GREEN - Lined properly for the Alliance Subdivision  
YELLOW - Lined properly for the Dallas Subdivision  
RED - STOP and inspect switch 
 
Wylie  
Main track switches may be left lined as last used.  
 
The east lead yard track is connected to the east end 
of the Wylie Intermodal Terminal track.  
 
When lining the switch(es) into or out of the Wylie  
Intermodal Terminal tracks, it will also be required to 
line the associated split rail derail in the non -derailing 
position.  
 
Power Assisted Switches (PAS): 
Alliance Jct. 
Radio Channel 010-010 
Normal DTMF #580411 Reverse DTMF #580422 
 
General Information 
Distributed Power  
Other than unit trains, westbound trains in excess of 
10,000 tons must have distributed power. 
 
Greenville  
1. If a red absolute signal is displayed at the DGNO  
Connection, at MP 171.2 the following will apply:  
 
a. After authority is granted by the control operator to 
pass the stop indication, the train crew must wait  5 
minutes 0 seconds then move by proper signal into 
the limits of the interlocking to insure the signals are 
at stop on the conflicting route.  
 
b. After waiting 6 minutes 0 seconds and no  
conflicting movement is seen or heard, movement 
may proceed on proper signal to the switches. 
Before passing over the switches, the train must 
stop, and the employee must operate the switches 
by hand as outline in Rule 9.13.1 (Hand Operation of 
Dual Control Switches).  
 
After at least one unit or car has passed over the  
switch points, the employee must return the  
switches to power unless otherwise instructed by  
the control operator.  
 
c. When movement is seen or heard on conflicting  
route, proceed signal must not be given until such  
movement is stopped.  
 
2. The interlocking signals at the CPKCR/Blackland RR  
crossing MP 170.2 are designated as control points.  
When a crew encounters a STOP signal at this location 
and fails to receive a proceed indication after following 
instructions in the release box, authority must be 
received from the train dispatcher before  proceeding, 
except when operating within the limits of track and 
time. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Welsh Power Plant  
Train crews operating empty coal trains will perform a  
Class IA air brake test prior to departing Hughes  
Springs If no extended haul brake slip is located in 
locomotive cab.  
Note: An extended haul brake test is now required after 
coal train arrives Kansas City. 
 
Baldwin  
MW 093 or 095 are prohibited.  
 
T&N Veals Yard  
Prior to entering the T&N yard at Veals, you must 
obtain permission from the T&N yardmaster on radio 
channel TX66-RX66 between the hours of 06:00 and 
18:00. 
 
If you receive no answer via radio during these hours,  
contact the train dispatcher for further instructions.  
 
All Tracks in the T&N yard will be restricted to 5 MPH. 
 
Hughes Springs  
A dual control derail has been installed on the East end  
of the siding. This derail operates in conjunction with 
the East dual control siding switch. When operating the 
East dual control switch by hand, it is also necessary 
to operate the derail by hand.  
 
In addition, a hand operated split derail has been 
installed on the East lead at the clearance point of the 
siding. For proper signal and dual control switch 
operation at East Hughes Springs, the derail must be 
in the derailing position.  
 
No loaded coal trains allowed on siding.  
 
Measured Mile: MP 196 - 197 and MP 80 - 81.  
 
Milepost Equalization:  
• East Fox:  MP 34.8 and MP 16.5 are the same 
location.  
• Alliance Junction: MP C-580.4 on the Alliance  
Subdivision and MP201.9 on the Dallas and Greenville  
Subdivisions are the same location.  
• West Leg Texas Wye:  0.7 on the Greenville 
Subdivision and MP Y -548.7 on the Shreveport 
Terminal Subdivision are the same location.  
• Texas Jct.: The south bound signal entering West  
Main off the Greenville Subdivision at MP 0.08 is the  
official Shreveport Terminal-Greenville Subdivision  
boundary.  
 
Note: Any bulletins requested from the switch point to  
the clearance point within the Texas Jct. turnout in  
Shreveport Terminal must be defined from MP 0.08  
to MP 0.0 (0.08 is the south bound signal entering  
West Main off the Greenville Subdivision; 0.0 is the  
switch point).

Switch Information 
Vicksburg Yard  
The following switches may be left as last lined:  
• The first switch approximately 50 feet north of 
Depot Street.  
 
Meridian  
Southern Crossover: All switches of crossover must be 
lined to establish block signal protection. After lining 
crossover switches, wait five (5) minutes before fouling 
crossover. 
 
Operation of East and West Lead Switches  
East Switch:  
Use channel 053-053 and enter the following codes:  
Normal position - #091011  
Reverse position - # 091022  
West Switch:  
Use channel 050-050 and enter the following codes:  
Normal position - #091311  
Reverse position - # 091322 
 
Koch Foods  
Dual control derails are located at the clearance point 
of each track. These derails are operated in 
conjunction with both the main and industry track dual-
control switches operated by the train dispatcher. 
When required to operate either dual control switch by 
hand, it is also necessary to hand operate the derail for 
the track you will enter. 
 
Peco Foods  
A dual control derail is installed on the industry track. 
This derail operates in conjunction with the siding 
switch. When operating the dual control switch by hand 
it is also necessary to operate the split point derail by 
hand.   
 
DTMF Yard Switches are installed on both the North 
Industry Track and South Industry Track of Peco Foods 
industry track. When entering the industry tracks it will 
be necessary to operate the DTMF switches.  
North Industry track switch DTMF code: normal switch 
DTMF #039811 – reverse switch DTMF #039822.   
South Industry track switch DTMF code: normal switch 
DTMF #039711 – reverse switch DTMF #039722. 
 
General Information 
The following restrictions apply to all manifest trains  
departing EWD from Vicksburg between MP 138.0 and  
MP 140.5: 
• Empty cars 85 feet or longer, empty flat cars, wood 
racks and empty chip hoppers must be handled 
with no more than 7,000 trailing tons behind such 
cars.  
 
 
 
• EWD trains that stall between MP 140.5 and MP 
139 must not attempt to start train without helpers 
or distributed power.  
• No more than 30 equivalent powered axles may 
be used on the head-end of the train and no more 
than 20 powered axles may be used on helpers or 
distributed power.  
• Trains operating with excess of 7,000 trailing tons 
must have ten (10) loads (cars weighing over 50 
tons) on the head end or be operated with 
distributed power or helper locomotives. 
 
Vicksburg Yard  
The following switches may be left as last lined:  
• Double stack Intermodal Cars and Autoracks will 
not clear under Fairground Street Bridge in 
Vicksburg Yard. 
 
Mississippi River Bridge – Vicksburg, MS MP 142.5  
A bridge strike alarm monitors the bridge for water 
vessel impacts.  If the CDU denotes that the alarm has 
been activated, trains must stop short of the bridge or 
bring train to a stop with proper train handling if already 
traversing the bridge.  Once stop ped, trains must 
remain stopped until Bridge Authority clears the bridge 
for movement.   
 
Key Trains Between MP 138 And MP 140.3  
Key trains or cut of cars meeting the definition of a Key  
Train must not be left unattended between MP 138.0 
and MP 140.3.  
 
Between MP 138 and MP 140.5  
When approaching 10-degree curve at MP 139.7, be  
governed by ABTH Rule 104.3.2 B Dynamic Brake  
Limitations.   
 
When train air brakes are required to reduce or control  
speed, the following will govern:  
• If necessary to use train air brakes to reduce and 
maintain speed through this location the brakes 
must be applied sufficiently in advance to require 
no more than a minimum reduction to reduce train 
speed with throttle no higher than number 3 
position.  
• Do not exceed the throttle position in relation to the 
number of equivalent axles of power as follows:  
 
Number of axles   Maximum Throttle Position  
Less than 18  4  
18 or more  3  
 
Meridian 
All trains must contact Meridian Yard prior to entering 
yard limits.  
 
Jackson  
Inbound trains must contact Jackson Yard and receive  
permission to enter.  
 
Trains must not block Pearson Road or Deeb Street  
Crossings on the Meridian Subdivision. Trains being 
held out of Jackson Yard are to stop short of these two 
crossings.  
 
Be governed by GCOR 5.13 (Blue Signal Protection) 
when protecting workmen on this track, also governed 
by ABTH Section 3, Rule 28.1.  
 
US Southern Region Timetable 
MERIDIAN SUBDIVISION  67  July 1, 2024 
 
 
This track may be used under the direction of the 
supervisor in charge of Jackson Yard. 
 
Switching Signals at Jackson  
Before the train dispatcher may line the crossover from 
the switching lead to Main No. 2 at Jackson for 
movement through the crossover, or set any switching 
signal to a Stop indication, the dispatcher must contact 
the Manager on Duty. The Manager on Duty must verify 
that no train or switching job is using the signal and/or 
that they will remain clear of the signal. 
 
Milepost Equalization:  
• MP 135.0 on the Artesia Subdivision and MP 0.0 on 
the Meridian Subdivision are the same location. 
 
---END---

Broken Rail Detection (BRD)  
Broken Rail Detection (BRD) limits are in effect on the  
main track between MP230.0 and MP222.0 and 
between MP215.5 and MP137.1.  
 
Begin BRD and End BRD signs will be posted at the 
outer limits of BRD Territory.  
 
Limits monitored by BRD have indicators that display  
aspects for the condition of the track. 
 
BRD Indicators  
Aspect   Indication  
Flashing Green  No defects  
Flashing Red  Expect next indicator to be red  
Red or Dark  Proceed at restricted speed until the 
leading wheels pass the next BRD  
indicator and report to the train 
dispatcher.  
 
While moving within BRD territory, trains must comply 
with the indication of the BRD indicator.  
 
If an indicator displaying a flashing green or flashing 
red changes to an indication requiring a train to 
proceed at restricted speed, the train must immediately 
reduce speed consistent with good train handling. Train 
must then move at restricted speed unt il the leading 
wheels pass the next BRD indicator and report such an 
indicator change to the train dispatcher.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
When one of the following occurs, move at restricted  
speed until the leading wheels have passed the next  
BRD indicator or the end of BRD limits:  
• The train enters the main track between BRD  
indicators.  
• The previous BRD indicator is unknown.  
• Movements in the opposite direction from which 
the BRD segment was entered.

AUTOMATIC INTERLOCKING INSTRUCTIONS  
If Home Signal Fails to Display a Proceed Indication:  
1. Operate button on signal mast at home signal and

after waiting 5 minutes:  
a) Place first derail in hand position and line for rail  
traffic. Proceed over derail on proper signal from  
crew member.  
b) After one unit or one car has passed over first

c)  Ascertain from the Bridge Tender or by a member

derail on proper signal from crew member.  
e)  After one unit or one car has passed over second  
derail, restore derail to Power position.

CPKC-Up Joint Track Between MP 735.6 Lettsworth

UP employees will be governed by the G COR, CPKC

Labarre  
The west track is designated as the siding.  
 
Lobdell - Baton Rouge Terminal Area  
1. Trains doubling over the Mississippi River Bridge 
(MP 783.2) must not leave any part of the train on the  
steel structure.  
 
CPKC dispatcher controls CTC between East Junction  
(MP 784.8 and North Lobdell MP 779.1).  
 
Northward trains must contact yardmaster before  
passing South Essen – MP 795.4.  
All Northward movements entering CTC at East  
Junction, MP 784.8, must obtain verbal permission  
from CPKC train dispatcher.  
 
Southward trains must contact CPKC train dispatcher  
for TWC authority before leaving Baton Rouge.  
 
Do not exceed five (5) MPH from West Jct. Switch to  
West Switch at Port Yard  
 
Southward Trains and Engines must contact Baton  
Rouge Yardmaster before entering Yard Limit at East  
Jct. MP 784.8. 
 
Bridge Junction  
The switch at Bridge Junction, Mile Post 785.2, is  
operated by radio control (DTMF CONTROLLED) and  
is equipped with a switch point indicator as defined  
by GCOR Rule 8.10.  
 
To line the switch for the Main Line use road channel  
010-010 and press in code #785211.  
 
To line the switch for the “D” Line use road channel  
010-010 and press in code #785222.  
 
Switch Point Indicator at the switch will indicate the  
switch positions as follows: 
  
GREEN light will indicate switch is lined for the Main 
Line.  
YELLOW light will indicate switch is lined for the “D” 
Line.  
RED light will indicate switch is not lined or out of 
correspondence and movement must be stopped short 
of the switch.  
 
When a Red indicator light is encountered the switch 
must be operated by hand. If necessary to operate the 
switch by hand, do not restore the switch to power 
operation until at least one unit or car has passed over 
the switch points. When a train or engine is within 300 
feet of the switch, the switch will be locked and cannot 
be operated by radio control. The switch can be left 
lined as last used.

 2. “D” Line Operations: MP D -209.7 - D-221.4: All

3. UTL lead off “D” Line, MP D-216.0 begins the Baton  
Rouge Southern Railroad.  
 
CN RRX at MP 787.4 is protected by a gate. 
 
Norco  
1. The first road crossing north of the south siding 
switch at Norco, commonly referred to as the “Rubber”  
crossing, serves the Shell Oil Company Polypropylene  
Plant and must not be blocked with cars. Cars set out  
by through trains must be left clear of this crossing.  
2. Do not exceed five (5) MPH over Norco Plant Lead.  
3. Do not exceed five (5) MPH over L&A 3 and 4.  
4. Do not exceed five (5) MPH inside CII Carbon Plant 
at Norco.  
 
Diamond Green  
North and South Diamond Green are equipped with  
Radio Control Switches (RCS). These switches can be  
controlled by DTMF on the radio keypad, or by using a  
push button located at the switches.  
 
These switches will restore to the normal position 60  
seconds after movement has been made through the  
limits of the OS. Movement over the switches will be  
governed by ABS signals. At RCS locations, there will 
be signals marking the limits of the OS. For the RCS to 
operate by DTMF or by push button located at the 
switch, the limits of the OS must not be occupied. Do 
not exceed 5 MPH while weighing cars on Dia mond 
Green.  
 
Operating a Radio-Controlled Switch:  
1. To operate a Radio-Controlled Switch (RCS), a crew  
member must perform the following:  
Upon passing the wayside sign reading "switch  
control" placed for South bound trains at MP 846.17  
and for North bound trains at MP 850.87, a crew  
member must enter the proper DTMF sequence for  
the desired switch position for BOTH North and 
South Diamond Green.  
 
2. A train must approach a Radio-Controlled Switch  
prepared to stop short of the OS until:  
A. A DTMF command has been issued to request the  
switch for the desired position.  
and  
B. The ABS signal approaching the Radio Controlled  
Switch displays a more favorable aspect than  
approach.  
or  
C. The signal at the switch displays that the switch is  
properly lined for movement.  
 
3. If the train has not passed the signal at the requested  
switch within 15 minutes after entering the proper  
DTMF sequence, the train must approach the Radio  
Controlled Switch prepared to stop.  
 
 
4. If a change is needed from the original requested  
route, the train must stop outside the limits of the OS  
at the Radio-Controlled Switch and:  
A. Wait 15 minutes then enter the proper DTMF  
sequence for the desired position,  
or  
B. Wait 15 minutes and operate the push button  
located on the signal case to line the switch for  
the desired position.  
NOTE: Permission to operate the dual control switch 
by hand in accordance with GCOR Rule 9.13.1 is 
granted without having to contact the control operator. 
 
5. If the signal approaching a Radio-Controlled Switch  
displays a more favorable aspect than approach  
and the Radio -Controlled Switch signal displays a 
red or dark aspect, the crew must:  
A. Stop the train before entering the OS if consistent  
with good train handling  
B. Inspect the switch  
and  
C. Report it to the control operator  
NOTE: Permission to operate the dual control switch 
by hand in accordance with GCOR Rule 9.13.1 is 
granted, but the control operator must be notified of the 
signal indication.  
 
6. If after entering the proper DTMF sequence, the  
signal continues to display a stop indication and the  
train is authorized beyond the signal, the train has  
permission to pass the stop indication at restricted  
speed without contacting the control operator, only  
after operating the RCS by hand.  
 
7. The industry track switch in the scale track at  
Diamond Green operates in conjunction with the  
South main line switch (i.e., if entering the code to  
occupy the scale track or industry track, the main  
line switch and the switch in the scale track will both  
line and lock for movement into the designated  
route.)  
NOTE: Only one of the three codes needs to be 
entered for a given route at South Diamond Green.  
 
Movement across CNIC Track from Frellsen Jct. To 
CPKC New Orleans  
Baton Rouge: Southward trains before departing Baton  
Rouge for New Orleans must have a copy of current 
CN Daily Operating Bulletins for the McComb and 
Baton Rouge Districts. Train crews will verify Daily 
Operating Bulletin number(s) with CN Rail Traffic 
Controller (RTC) and have permission from CN Mays 
Yard before passing South Frellsen.  
 
New Orleans Yard: Northward trains departing New  
Orleans must have a copy of the current CN Daily  
Operating Bulletins for the McComb and Baton Rouge  
Districts. Train crews will verify Daily Operating Bulletin  
number with CN RTC and have permission from CN 
Mays Yard before departing New Orleans Yard.  
 
All trains must keep radio on CN Channel 054 -054 
while operating on CN track. The CN train RTC can be  
contacted on this channel.

CN Chief Dispatcher FAX .................... (708) 206-6775   
 
New Orleans Yard  
1. The train dispatcher will issue TWC authority to  
northward trains before arriving Frellsen Jct. This will  
not modify or supersede rules or instructions  
governing operation via CN but permits trains to  
depart New Orleans yard after verbal authority is  
obtained to enter CN CTC territory.  
 
2. CPKC train and engine movements between 
Frellsen JCT and CPKC New Orleans yard will be 
made via CN railroad and east bridge interlocker. Be 
governed by CN Operating Rules, CN Timetable and 
special instructions, and CN TGBO.  
 
3. The Maximum Authorized Speed through the turnout  
in the East Bridge interlocking is 10 MPH.  
 
4. CPKC train movements between New Orleans yard  
and the NOPB’s Cotton Warehouse yard will be  
made via the CN Railroad at Lambert Jct. for  
approximately 1800 feet to the NOPB connection.  
Movements via this route will be controlled by and  
authorized by East Bridge Tower. CN Operating 
Rules will govern CPKC train movements between 
Lambert Junction and NOPB Connection. NOPB 
General Code of Operating Rules, Timetable, 
General Orders and Bulletins will govern CPKC train 
movements while occupying NOPB.  
 
5. All movements between Lambert Junction and  
Southport will be made per GCOR 6.28.  
 
6. All tracks at Cotton Warehouse Yard, located at  
NOPB New Orleans are designated as interchange  
tracks for CPKC interchange to CSXT Railroad.  
 
NOTE: Do not exceed 8,000 feet for CSXT train in New  
Orleans.

The drawbridge is a manual interlocking controlled by

UP Interlocking Instructions - Beaumont  
Trains and engines encountering a STOP indication at 
the UP interlocking located at MP 769.8, after verifying 
that signals on the conflicting route indicate STOP and 
no conflicting movement is evident, may proceed 
through the interlocking at Restricted Speed. When 
signals on the conflicting route do not indicate STOP 
and conflicting movement is evident, train or engine 
must not proceed until both crews agree on the next 
movement.

Switch Information 
Madden  
Dual control derails are installed on the Madden 
industry tracks. These derails operate in conjunction 
with the main line switches. When operating the North 
dual control switch by hand it is also necessary to 
operate the switch point derail by hand. When 
operating the South dual control switch by hand it is 
also necessary to operate the switch point derail by 
hand.   
 
DTMF Yard Switches are installed on both ends of 
Madden industry track. When entering the industry 
tracks it will be necessary to operate the DTMF 
switches.   
 
North industry track switch DTMF code: normal switch 
to 702 Track DTMF #595511 – reverse switch to 701 
Track DTMF #595522.   
 
 
South industry track switch DTMF code: normal switch 
to 702 Track DTMF #596111 – reverse switch to 701 
Track DTMF #596122. 
 
Neches Junction  
DTMF Yard Switches are installed on the Neches 
Junction North Wye, Neches Junction East Wye, and 
Neches Junction South Wye. When approaching a 
Wye Yard switch, it will be necessary to operate the 
DTMF switches.  
 
Neches Junction North Wye switch DTMF code:  
normal switch DTMF #779211 – reverse switch DTMF 
#779222.  
 
Neches Junction East Wye switch DTMF code: normal 
switch (South Leg) DTMF #779311 – reverse switch 
(North Leg) DTMF #779322.  
 
Neches Junction South Wye switch DTMF code: 
normal switch DTMF #779511 – reverse switch DTMF 
#779522.  
 
South USA Rail Terminal  
A DTMF Yard Switch is installed for the USA Rail 
Terminal.  A power derail is installed on the industry 
track that works in  conjunction with the main line 
switch.  If necessary to operate the main line switch by 
hand, the derail must also be operated by hand.  When 
entering the industry track it will be necessary to 
operate the DTMF switches.   
DTMF code: normal switch DTMF #780511 – reverse 
switch DTMF #780522. 
 
Jefferson Refinery  
A dual control derail is installed on the industry track. 
This derail operates in conjunction with the dual control 
main line switch. When operating the main line switch 
by hand it is also necessary to operate the derail by 
hand.  
 
Beaumont  
Signals and dual control switches between Langham 
Road and Wall Street and between South Street and 
Crockett Street are controlled by UP control operators. 
 
Sunoco  
Dual control derail is installed on the industry track. 
This derail operates in conjunction with the main line 
PAS switch.  
 
When operating the PAS switch by hand, it is also  
necessary to operate the power derail by hand. 
 
Port Neches Branch and Belt Line  
The switch to SLIC track 700, must be lined and locked 
for the Port Neches Belt Line when not in use. The 
normal position of this switch will be lined to go toward 
Pab-Tex.  
 
A DTMF Yard Switch is installed for the Port Arthur 
Terminal.  A power derail is installed on the lead track 
that works in conjunction with the main line switch.  If 
necessary to operate the main line switch by hand, the 
derail must also be operated by han d.  When entering 
the lead track, it will be necessary to operate the DTMF 
switches.   
DTMF code: Normal DTMF #005811 – Reverse DTMF 
#005822.

General Information 
Fort Polk Military Base  
Fort Polk Military Base has installed an electric security 
gate at the track entrance to the Fort Polk base, 
Milepost 3.5 at Highway 467. The gate will 
automatically open when a train is within 400 feet of 
either side of gate. All trains must be prepared t o stop 
at the gate until the gate is fully open. The gate may 
only be manually operated from inside the base 
through the use of a manual switch located inside the  
gate. 
 
Dequincy  
Number 1 Track (south leg of the wye) at DeQuincy is 
other than main track.  
 
Trains moving via Number 1 Track at DeQuincy must 
be within fifty (50) feet of either side of Louisiana 
Highway 12 (Fourth Street) to activate highway 
crossing warning devices.  
 
Lemonville  
Trains and engines will not exceed 5 MPH within 2,000 
feet of the north and south switches to the SRN 
interchange tracks.   
 
CPKC trains and engines may enter and occupy SRN 
tracks at Lemonville (within 2,000 feet of the north and 
south switches to the SRN interchange tracks) without 
flag protection.  
 
Foreign Line Trains And Engines  
Foreign line trains must receive and verify CPKC Track 
Bulletin before entering the main track at CS Junction 
MP 720.3, Tower 31 MP 764.8, and Station 11 (Wall 
Street) MP 766.9. CPKC does not issue track warrants 
for bulletins.  
 
Contact CPKC Train Dispatcher (refer to System 
Special Instructions for phone number) to establish 
signal indication, or obtain verbal authority, to enter 
CTC at CS Junction, Tower 31, or Station 11. 
 
Beaumont  
SWD trains on CPKC Beaumont Subdivision operating 
via Chaison Yard must obtain verbal permission from 
the CPKC Yardmaster before departing Vidor and 
before departing Chaison Yard southbound.  
 
NWD trains must obtain verbal permission from the 
CPKC Yardmaster and CPKC Train Dispatcher before 
departing Chaison Yard.  
EWD trains on UP Lafayette Subdivision operating via  
Chaison Yard must obtain verbal permission from the 
CPKC Yardmaster before departing Wall Street and 
before departing Chaison Yard southbound. 
 
Port Arthur  
Northward trains departing Port Arthur must receive 
verbal permission from the Yardmaster at Port Arthur 
before departing Port Arthur yard.  
 
 
 
 
No six axle locomotives or loaded unit trains on track 
532 (zero track).  
 
Port Arthur Remote Operations  
Port Arthur has been established as a Remote Control  
Operating Area.  
 
A Remote-control zone is established on the North end 
of the Port Arthur Yard on the work lead between the  
clearance point of the middle track, and the south  
roundhouse (18 track) switch.  This zone shall be 
identified as RCZ1.  
 
A Remote -Control Zone is established on the south 
end of the Port Arthur Yard on the work lead between 
county road crossing, zero track switch and 18 switch.  
This zone shall be identified as RCZ2. 
 
Port Arthur Roundhouse  
Power operated derails, equipped with blue lights, are  
located at the north and south ends of the diesel shop.  
 
To enter the limits of the blue signal:  
• If blue signal is displayed, the employee must 
contact locomotive servicing personnel for 
permission to enter the limits. The employee must 
verify the derail is in the non -derailing position 
before entering the limits.  
• If blue signal is not displayed, the employee must 
contact the yardmaster to determine if locomotive 
servicing personnel are on duty. If locomotive 
servicing personnel are on duty, the employee 
must receive permission from the locomotive 
servicing personne l to enter the limits. If 
locomotive servicing personnel are not on duty, 
the employee may enter the limits after verifying 
the derail is in the non-derailing position.  
 
Before moving a locomotive within the limits of the blue  
signal, the employee must receive permission from  
locomotive servicing personnel. If unable to contact  
locomotive servicing personnel, determine from the  
yardmaster if locomotive servicing personnel are on 
duty. If no locomotive servicing personnel are on duty, 
the employee may move the locomotive. The 
employee must verify the derail is in the non -derailing 
position before departing the limits.  
 
---END---

BROKEN RAIL DETECTION (BRD) 
Broken Rail Detection (BRD) limits are in effect on the 
main track between MP 0.34 and MP 04.16. 
 
Begin BRD and End BRD signs will be posted at the 
outer limits of BRD Territory. 
 
Limits monitored by BRD have indicators that display 
aspects for the condition of the track. 
US Southern Region Timetable  
 
LAREDO SUBDIVISION  105  July 1, 2024 
 
 
BRD INDICATORS 
Aspect Indication 
Flashing 
Green No Defects 
Flashing Red Expect next indication to be red 
Red or Dark Proceed at restricted speed until 
the leading wheels pass the next 
BRD indicator and report to the 
Train Dispatcher 
 
While moving within BRD territory, trains must comply 
with the indication of the BRD indicator. 
 
If an indicator displaying a flashing green or flashing 
red changes to an indication requiring a train to 
proceed at restricted speed, the train must immediately 
reduce speed consistent with good train handling. 
Train must then move at restricted speed until the 
leading wheels pass the next BRD indicator and report 
such an indicator change to the train dispatcher. 
 
When one of the following occurs, move at restricted 
speed until the leading wheels have passed the next 
BRD indicator or the end of BRD limits: 
 
• The train enters the main track between BRD 
indicators. 
• The previous BRD indicator is unknown. 
• Movements in the opposite direction from which 
the BRD segment was entered.
